data.business: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing across multiple product categories. The group primarily operates on a cash and carry business model alongside sales to subsidiaries, making credit risk from receivables insignificant. The company operates brick-and-mortar stores alongside an online shopping service called DMart Ready.
data.narrative: The annual report highlights DMart's footprint expansion to 500 stores with 20.58 million square feet of retail business area as of March 31, 2026, operating on a low credit risk cash and carry model. On recent concalls, management agrees with this operational scale while placing greater emphasis on store ownership dynamics, noting that 68 out of 500 stores are leased and that DMart owns approximately 88% of its properties. Management also brings into focus operational headwinds not detailed in high-level financial summaries, such as warehousing rental inflation, wage pressures, deteriorated fixed asset turnover due to rising real estate costs, and managing the online DMart Ready service separately.

bull.point: DMart has steadily expanded its retail footprint to 500 stores encompassing 20.58 million square feet of retail business area by March 31, 2026.
The company operates a low credit risk cash and carry business model, driving turnover to close to INR 67,000 crores without defaulting on any borrowing obligations.
The DMart Ready e-commerce platform delivered 21% to 22% sales growth, operating across 24 cities with 165 pickup points.
Operational stability is supported by high property ownership of approximately 88% and a reduction in employee attrition from 13.9% to 11.3%.

bear.point: Escalating per-location real estate prices and accelerated property acquisitions have increased capital employed and deteriorated return on capital and fixed asset turnover.
Non-store operational costs are rising due to rapid inflation in warehousing rentals, employee wage increases, and higher transportation costs from a shift toward home delivery.
DMart Ready e-commerce operates at an EBITDA loss of minus 2% to minus 3%, recording a loss of INR 247 crores in FY2025.
Short-term borrowings reached 965.27 Crores while cash and cash equivalents net of overdrawn bank balances ended at negative 96.56 Crores as of March 31, 2026.

data.balance: As of March 31, 2026, short-term borrowings stood at 965.27 Crores, while cash and cash equivalents net of bank overdrawn balances were negative 96.56 Crores, supported by 169.17 Crores in undrawn committed borrowing facilities. For the year ended March 31, 2026, net cash flow generated from operating activities was 3,466.74 Crores, while net cash flow used in investing activities was 4,206.96 Crores.
